name: Fix the cardinality of cross-round pairing so a moved finding pairs on an ensemble head
description:
Split out of CZ3TDR1-725. That ticket got rule codes onto the standard contract and met its first "Done when" (every model attaches a code — measured 9 of 9 on the drill). Its second and third — a moved finding pairs whichever model reported it, and a problem the partner already holds open does not get a second thread — are **not** met, and cannot be met without changing the pairing itself, which CZ3TDR1-725 deliberately put out of scope.

## What is wrong

The pairing group is `(path, rule_code)` and is blind to which model reported the finding. `orphanedPrior` counts `group.members`, which are **locations**, where the predicate's own wording says **findings** (`apps/worker/src/jobs/reconcile-findings.ts:1935`), and the pairing fires only at "exactly one prior and exactly one current" (`:1980`).

Before rule codes reached the standard contract, one problem reported by both models split across a coded group and a NULL group, so the coded half had one prior and one current and paired. Now both models cite the same code, both halves land in one group, the group holds two of each, and the pairing declines for both.

**Measured on the drill**, `roman-talas-snowly-code/st-addon-drill-moved`, from `action_logs` in the local stack:

The XSS blocker in `src/render.js` after the change: round 1 has `claudecode :6 A1` and `stskill :6 A1`; round 2 has `claudecode :44 A1` and `stskill :96 A1`. Two prior, two current, one group.

Worth stating so the severity is not read too high or too low: on the drill itself this is a wash, because the pre-change NULL group held three findings and never paired either — all three pairings that round sat on `stskill` rows. The regression is on the reconstructed shape of **a file with a single moved finding**, where both groups used to hold one prior and one current, both carriers were recognised, and `crossRoundSuppressed` held the canonical back. That shape was verified by running the predicate, not observed on the drill.

**Two conditions narrow it further.** It needs both rounds to carry the same known `rule_set_version` — `resetReviewForRequeue` (`packages/db/src/reviews-write.ts:458`) nulls it on every requeue, and a NULL on either side makes the tiebreak drop the code anyway. And the partner-facing half only happens once `carried_over_enabled` is on; the switch defaults off (`getCarriedOverEnabled`, `packages/db/src/engine-settings.ts`) and gates `loadCarriedOver` in both `judge-pr.ts` and `outbound-send.ts`.

**Half of the damage is already closed** by CZ3TDR1-725's fail-safe: when the pairing declines with orphans on both sides, the prior entries are marked `refoundAmbiguously` and the roll-up will not close the finding (`reconcile-findings.ts:1980-1984`, `:2054`). So the failure mode left is a duplicate thread, not a wrongly closed finding — the cheaper side of the axis this feature is built around, but still the promise the batch exists to keep.

## Inherited with that safeguard: one surviving mutant on its counter

This ticket owns `refoundAmbiguously`, because fixing the cardinality is what removes the need for it — so the gap below comes here rather than staying on CZ3TDR1-725, and PR #77's description points at this ticket for it.

`reconcile-findings.ts:2148` reads:

```ts
if (ambiguous && !isReanchored && bucketsClosed) totals.refoundAmbiguously++;
```

Drop `!isReanchored` and the whole suite still passes — re-verified on 2026-09-29 against the current head: 136/136 in `reconcile-findings.test.ts`. The mutant is **not** equivalent. A judge canonical that expands to several covered locations can have one group pair 1:1 (so `movedTo` is set and `isReanchored` is true) while another pairs ambiguously (so `ambiguous` is true). In that state the real code does not count and the mutant does.

**The behaviour is right; the test is missing.** The intent is stated in the counter's own docblock — "Counted where it CHANGED the answer, not wherever the flag is set" — and the impact of the gap is a number in a log line, nothing partner-facing. It is recorded because a safeguard whose counter nobody checks is how the next person mis-reads a production log.

A test for it wants a canonical covering two locations in two different `(path, rule_code)` groups, one paired 1:1 and one ambiguous, asserting `reconcileTotal("refoundAmbiguously")` is 0. Whoever does the cardinality work is in that code anyway; if the fix retires the counter, delete this instead.

## Two candidates, with the trade-off that makes this its own ticket

- **Count findings on the prior side and canonical groups on the current side.** Faithful to the predicate's wording; the judge has already ruled that the covered rows are one problem, and `crossRoundSuppressed`'s `every` then has all its carriers. Cost: if the judge consolidates a re-find with a genuinely new finding of the same rule in the same file, both get linked and both get suppressed — a MISS, the direction this feature leans away from.
- **Put the provider in the group key.** No consolidation risk. Cost: a cross-provider re-find stops pairing — model X reports it in round 1, model Y in round 2 — which with two models this divergent is not a rare shape.

The first looks better: its miss needs the judge to be wrong about two findings being one problem, while the second's cost lands on ordinary model flakiness. Not decided here.

## Scope note

The current side is the expensive half. `currentRows` is loaded with `notJudgeRow()` (`reconcile-findings.ts:1507-1527`), so the pairing loop has no canonical coverage data at all today; option one needs a new query for it, and the link write at `:2019` sets `continuesCommentId` on a single row and would have to set it on several. The prior side is small — deduplicate `orphanedPrior` by `finding.id`.

**Done when:** a moved finding pairs on an ensemble head whichever model reported it, a problem the partner is already holding open does not get a second thread, the drill shape above shows non-zero `links` after the change, and the `refoundAmbiguously` counter is either held by a test or retired with the safeguard.
